newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH LIFE INSURANCE Q2 TURNOVER LOWER - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH LIFE INSURANCE Q2 TURNOVER LOWER - PAPER.

text.p: French life insurance turnover continued its decline in the second quarter, sliding eight percent, according to a study by the French insurance federation, the newspaper L'Agefi reported on Thursday.
The drop followed a two percent fall in the first quarter.

The newspaper said the preliminary study covered only half the members of the Federation Francaise des Societes d'Assurances. Final figures would only be known in the second half of August but were unlikely to differ much from the preliminary estimate, it said.
The federation said it could not confirm the newspaper's figures.
The estimate reflected a continuation of a falling trend in life insurance turnover witnessed in the second half of last year, the newspaper said.

Life insurance turnover in 1996, which totalled 535 billion francs, was only swelled by a shift away from tax-free savings Livret A savings schemes after the government cut interest rates on the state-guaranteed deposits by one percentage point to 3.5 percent.
The government's move followed complaints by commercial banks of unfair competition.
Life insurance turnover jumped 21.7 percent in the first half of 1996 but advanced 0.5 percent in the second half.

The newspaper said the impact of the shift away from Livret A accounts into life insurance products masked a problem for life insurance which probably dated from 1995 and the previous conservative government's first attacks on the tax advantages enjoyed by life insurance products.

Also, the new strength of the stock market has made the popularity of life insurance contracts wane along with the election of the new Socialist government which has raised worries about possible moves to limit tax benefits enjoyed by such products that include inheritance tax exemption.
The newspaper said 76.1 percent of life insurance contracts were savings plans while only 5.8 percent were for use in event of death.
Up to now, life insurance has been considered not as insurance but as tax-free method of savings, the newspaper noted.
Another factor hitting life insurance turnover was an increase in 1990 in the minimum length of life insurance contracts to eight years from six years, the newspaper said.
The apparent decline in the popularity of life insurance contracts has implications for the bond market as most of the money is invested in bonds.
